page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v6 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features two dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon 8573C core operating at clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The underlying x86_64 processor architecture includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI.

Because the instance relies on a single dual-threaded core, multi-threaded performance scales moderately compared to larger instances. Benchmark evaluations reflect this architectural ceiling, with multi-core throughput in stress-ng (1991.89) and Geekbench (2104.0) placing in the lower percentiles. Conversely, single-threaded throughput benefits from the high clock speeds, as shown by strong gzip compression performance of 31.33 GB/sec and average Geekbench single-core results of 1709.0. Memory throughput reaches 20.8 GB/sec for uncached reads and 14.3 GB/sec for uncached writes.

The D2s_v6 includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached disks and virtual networking configuration for production deployments. Additionally, it contains no hardware GPU accelerators. Given its resource density and hardware profile, this instance offers a cost-effective operational baseline for lightweight microservices, small background workers, API endpoints, low-traffic web serving, and basic CI/CD utility workloads.

Based on the x86_64 architecture, the processor integrates modern vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote managed disks. Benchmark metrics show competitive single-core execution, demonstrated by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.33 GB/sec and average Geekbench single-core performance. Multi-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth reflect the limitations of a two-thread topology. The D2s_v6 offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile suitable for low-scale web serving, light containerized microservices, development environments, and small background tasks.
